title: Elazar ben Charsom, the High Priest
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: According to the Rambam in his [Introduction to Zera’im](https://www.sefaria.org/Rambam_Introduction_to_the_Mishnah.23.2), he lived in the time of Antigenos, but Hyman says, “We have found no source at all for this,” for according to the narratives of Yosippon, after Shimon HaTzaddik came Elazar his brother, after him Menashe his uncle, and after him Shimon HaTzaddik’s son named Chonyo, as High Priests — unless, Hyman says, we say that he was a serving Kohen in Antigenos’s time, as we explained in the entry Shimon HaTzaddik. In [Yoma 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.9a.5) it is mentioned that he was High Priest for eleven years, and there, at [35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.35b.5), it is related that his mother made him a tunic worth twenty thousand [dinars], and his fellow priests did not let him wear it because he looked naked in it. [It is related of him there](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.35b.9-10) that his father left him great wealth, and he did not benefit from his wealth; he would carry a sack of flour on his shoulders and go from city to city to study Torah. Once his servants found him and pressed him into forced labor, for they did not recognize him. And where he is mentioned as Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom, Hyman calls this a habit of language, for in his time they were not yet called “Rabbi.” Likewise in [Kiddushin 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.49b.3) he is mentioned as an example of great wealth. [They said in Yoma there](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.35b.13): “Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom makes the wealthy answerable.”[^1][^2][^3][^4]

notes.text: Yoma describes the tunic as worth two myriads. The Davidson edition supplies dinars. [Hyman’s printed text](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=207) reads “tunic” and “it is told of him.”
Yoma introduces the eleven years of service as an alternative tradition.

Rambam groups Elazar and Antigonos together without dating Elazar’s service. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=496&lang=en) also places him in Antigonos’s time. This entry cites Yosippon, whose [consulted chapter 17](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yosifun/yosifun04.pdf#page=4) names Eleazar in Ptolemy’s story separately from the high priest in Jerusalem. In his [entry on Shimon HaTzaddik](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=390), Hyman cites [Josephus, Antiquities 12.43 and 12.157–158](https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Josephus/ant-12.html) for the succession. The precise Yosippon passage behind Hyman’s citation remains uncertain.

The Bavli and Hyman’s printed quotation give Charsom (חרסום). The supplied Hebrew transcription has Charsim (חרסים) in the final line. The maxim holds the wealthy answerable for neglecting Torah study.
